meta.title: Bulls and Cows — Training Mode Knowledge Packet
meta.source: Wikipedia, Tetsuro Tanaka (1996), Goel & Garg (2015), n1b-algo research (2012), MOO Strategies paper
meta.game_variant: 4-digit, distinct digits, digits 0-9 (first digit may be 0)

scoring.win_condition: 4 bulls (all digits correct and in correct position)

proven_statistics.source: Tetsuro Tanaka, University of Tokyo, Game Programming Workshop 1996
proven_statistics.note_on_worst_case: No algorithm can guarantee solving in ≤6 turns for all 5040 codes; 7 is the proven minimum upper bound

turn_distribution.description: Estimated distribution for optimal strategy. Modelled to satisfy: sum=5040 games, weighted mean=26274/5040≈5.21. Exact per-turn counts vary by algorithm.

human_player_scoring.description: Score and label assigned to a human player based on how many turns they took to solve. Benchmarked against the optimal strategy distribution.

scoring_table.label: Miraculous
scoring_table.context: Only 1 in 5040 codes can be solved on the first guess. Pure luck — but still extraordinary.

scoring_table.label: Exceptional
scoring_table.context: Top 0.2% of all possible games. Excellent first guess that dramatically narrowed the field.

scoring_table.label: Excellent
scoring_table.context: Top ~1.4% of games. Superb logical deduction — even optimal algorithms rarely finish this fast.

scoring_table.label: Very Good
scoring_table.context: Better than ~85% of all possible games. Strong, efficient play — well above average.

scoring_table.label: Good
scoring_table.context: Right at the optimal average of 5.21 turns. Solid, competent play. The modal outcome for expert algorithms.

scoring_table.label: Average
scoring_table.context: Within the normal human range. Even the best algorithms need 6 turns for ~36% of codes.

scoring_table.label: Below Average
scoring_table.context: The theoretical maximum. Only ~50 codes require this many turns under an optimal strategy. Room to improve.

scoring_table.label: Needs Practice
scoring_table.context: Beyond the proven maximum for optimal play. Likely a random-guessing approach without elimination strategy.

strategy_levels.description: Three tiers of play strategy, from beginner to optimal. Human players can be benchmarked against these.

level_1_novice.name: Random / Intuitive
level_1_novice.description: Player picks numbers without systematic elimination. May repeat digits already ruled out.
behaviours: Guesses numbers they 'like' without reasoning from feedback
Does not track which digits are confirmed or eliminated
May reuse digits already shown to be absent
Strategy changes only after getting 2-3 cows by luck

level_2_intermediate.name: Elimination / Pruning
level_2_intermediate.description: Player maintains a pruned set — eliminating impossible codes after each guess. Equivalent to randomly sampling from remaining possibilities.
behaviours: Tracks which digits are confirmed present/absent
Never repeats digits already ruled out
Picks next guess randomly from remaining valid codes
Shifts to permutation testing once positions are known
tips: After 0 bulls + 0 cows: all 4 digits are absent — eliminate them all
After getting cows: the digit is in the code but wrong position — try it elsewhere
After getting a bull: lock that digit in that position — don't move it

level_3_optimal.name: Minimax / Information Gain
level_3_optimal.description: Player (or algorithm) selects the guess that minimises the worst-case remaining possibilities — maximising information from each response.
key_principles: Each guess should partition the remaining solution space as evenly as possible
The best guess maximises information gain (minimises the largest remaining response class)
A guess need not be in the pruned set — a non-solution can still be the most informative guess
The minimax decision rule: always prefer the guess whose worst-case partition is smallest

human_friendly_algorithm.description: Simplified version of optimal strategy usable by humans without a computer
steps: Step 1: Start with a first guess that covers 4 distinct, spread digits — e.g. 0123 or 1234 or 5678
Step 2: After each response, mentally (or on paper) eliminate all codes that don't match the bulls+cows you received
Step 3: From remaining valid codes, count which digits appear most frequently across all positions
Step 4: Choose digits that appear LEAST frequently — these carry more new information
practical_tips: Your first guess should test 4 entirely new digits — you learn whether each of those 4 digits exists
Avoid starting with digits that repeat across guesses too early
Once you have 3+ bulls, there are usually only 3 possibilities left — enumerate them
4 cows on any guess means you have all 4 digits but in wrong positions — just permute them
2 bulls + 2 cows means 2 digits are locked; swap the other 2 to solve it in the next turn

known_strong_first_guesses.note: Most researched starting point; avg ~6.0 with naive follow-up
Common human starting guess; similar information value to 0123
Balanced digit spread; used in some solver implementations

algorithm_benchmarks.description: How different solving approaches compare. Use this to contextualise a human player's performance.

benchmarks.notes: Theoretical best. Uses full minimax search.
Selects guess by maximising entropy reduction. Near-optimal and computationally feasible.
Pick randomly among still-valid codes. Good human-equivalent baseline.
Always pick lowest remaining valid code. Slightly worse than random.
No strategy. Typical uninformed human first-time player.

how_to_use: After each game, record the number of turns the human player took
Look up `human_player_scoring.scoring_table` by turns to get score, label, percentile, and context string
Display the turn distribution graph with the player's result marked
Compare player's turns against `algorithm_benchmarks` to show which algorithmic tier they matched
If player took ≥6 turns, show `strategy_levels.level_2_intermediate.tips` as improvement hints
If player took ≤4 turns, celebrate with `label` and `context` from scoring table
Track across sessions: if player's average is trending toward 5.21, they are approaching optimal play
